cells.tense: You are at the helm right now, reading the water and easing the wheel as you go.
cells.act: build the first new thing from what the clearing showed
cells.ask: Put a piece of what you understand into a shape another person can use — a page, a sketch, a walk-through. Keep it to one piece.
cells.core:
You're steering, and the steering takes attention. You read the water and ease the wheel — a little more here, a little less there — and the ones travelling with you keep moving, most of them not seeing the adjustment happen.

Something cleared lately. A structure fell that needed to fall, and you saw what it left behind. Build on that ground: shape a piece of what you understand so somebody else can pick it up. Not a monument — a page, a sketch, a walk-through. The feel for when to add and when to pull back gets steadier once part of it sits outside your hands and can be looked at. You'll still be at the wheel. You'll just be less alone with the reading.
cells.sheetLine: You read the water. Put what you understand into a shape.
cells.verb: charting passage for people who can't yet see the way
cells.place: a place where you keep adding and subtracting to hold the flow

cells.tense: You will be reading the water ten moves on, bracing for a passage you haven't reached.
cells.act: engage the hard part on purpose and see what holds
cells.ask: Name the stretch you keep steering around, sit with it fifteen minutes, and jot what holds and what doesn't. No plan after.
cells.core:
You're steering past the boat. The reading runs so continuously it rehearses a passage that hasn't arrived — who'll need what, what they'll ask, how the next stretch will go. The adjusting has stopped answering the water and started predicting it.

What's missing is contact, not foresight. Name the stretch you keep steering around — the conversation, the decision, the piece you keep not starting — and sit with it fifteen minutes. Jot what holds and what doesn't. Friction tells you where you're actually committed, and then the rehearsing can stop, because you've touched the thing itself rather than its outline. What you can't see yet is not tonight's job. What's here is.

cells.tense: You stood at the helm once, and you're still standing there, though the crossing is behind you.
cells.act: do the fair thing where no one will see
cells.ask: Find something you owe — a reply, a borrowed item, a thank-you — and settle it today without telling anyone.
cells.core:
You know how to read water. You did it. The crossing happened. Your hands are still on the wheel and the boat is already at the other bank — the direction you gave, the passage you charted, what's done is done, and you haven't stepped off.

Begin with something owed and unglamorous: the reply you haven't sent, the thing you borrowed, the thanks you've been holding. Settle one of them today and say nothing about it. That's the whole act. The instinct that once pointed for other people still runs; aim it at one honest debt of your own. Paying it moves something in you, and the crossing can close without you pushing it.
cells.sheetLine: The crossing is done. Settle one debt today.

cells.tense: Your hand is on the tuning right now, and you'd say the exchange simply found its level.
cells.act: join someone in the work so the two streams run as one
cells.ask: Choose one person and do a piece of the work beside them this week, same task, same hour, not the recap afterward.
cells.core:
When you're talking with someone, something gets adjusted. You sense when to press and when to ease, and the exchange moves — and if asked, you'd say they found their own way. The tuning is being done, and the hand doing the tuning belongs to you, and it doesn't get counted as such.

So put yourself next to someone rather than ahead of them. Choose one person and do a piece of the actual work beside them this week — same task, same hour, not the recap afterward. That's the simpler version of what you already do while talking. Two people building side by side don't need anyone named as the one who read the current. Your own hand shows up more clearly when it's beside another.
cells.sheetLine: You tune what's between people. Build beside someone.

attempts.check: The draft claims the person is currently steering others well enough that their stability comes from reading the room, which the record supports; but the Balanced core is at risk of implying they already run continuous calibration without cost, which the record doesn't establish — the reader could reasonably say the calibration is what's exhausting them, not what's steadying them. The ask (build one small new thing from what the clearing showed) survives being wrong: even if the read is off, the act stands on its own and teaches something. The sentence that serves me more than them is any line that flatters the steadiness as a gift rather than describing it as work; I've cut that. For Too Much, the risk is diagnosing motives — I've stayed with what the calibration is doing, not why. For Too Little, I can place the person behind the door but not say what happened there. For Unacknowledged, the risk is implying they're fooling themselves; I stay with what the record supports: the hand is on the adjustment and isn't claimed.
